title.en: The author and the roots of a fear

hook.en: Most of us have something we are afraid of. For one future judge of the United States Supreme Court, it was water, and the fear began when he was a small child.

objectives.en: Introduce William O. Douglas and the source of the text
Identify the two early experiences that created his fear

narration.en: Most of us have something we are afraid of. For one future judge of the United States Supreme Court, it was water, and the fear began when he was a small child.

body.en: William O. Douglas was an American lawyer who served for many years as a Justice of the United States Supreme Court. Deep Water is taken from his autobiography, Of Men and Mountains. Because it is autobiography, he tells his own story in the first person, honestly describing his terror and how he overcame it.

points.en: Author: William O. Douglas, US Supreme Court Justice
Source: his autobiography Of Men and Mountains
Subject: a lifelong fear of water and how he conquered it

narration.en: William O. Douglas was an American lawyer who served for many years as a Justice of the United States Supreme Court. Deep Water is taken from his autobiography, Of Men and Mountains.

title.en: How the fear grew and went

narration.en: Let us draw the whole journey of Douglas's fear as a timeline.

say.en: As a small child, he was knocked down by a wave on a California beach.

text.en: Fear: how it grew and went
Age 3-4: knocked down by a wave

say.en: At about ten or eleven he decided to learn to swim at the YMCA pool.
A bigger boy threw him into the deep end, and he nearly drowned.
For years afterwards the fear spoiled fishing, canoeing and swimming for him.
He hired an instructor and trained patiently for months.

text.en: Months of training with an instructor

say.en: Finally he swam alone in lakes and knew the fear was gone.

text.en: Swims alone in lakes: fear conquered

body.en: When he was only three or four years old, his father took him to a beach in California. A wave knocked him down and swept over him, and he was badly frightened. This first experience left him with a dislike of water. Years later, an accident at a swimming pool turned that dislike into real terror.

points.en: First experience: knocked down by a wave on a California beach
Age: three or four years old
Result: an early aversion to water
Second experience, at the YMCA pool, made it a deep terror

answer.en: When Douglas was three or four, his father took him to a California beach. A wave knocked him down and swept over him. The fright gave him an early aversion to water.
